title: DW-MT322-WorkspaceVolumeProvisioning
group: DW Durable workspace volumes and handoff
clause: Named durable volume = raw ext4 image per workspace attached virtio-blk; disposable qcow2 delta boot disk with backing=base chain; worktree->VM->volume PostgreSQL bindings; durability-critical writes forbidden through virtio-fs

scope.summary:
GOAL: Give every agent workspace a Docker-volume-analog durable disk (research P7): one named durable volume per workspace as a raw ext4 image file attached virtio-blk, plus a per-workspace DISPOSABLE qcow2 delta boot disk whose backing file is an MT-321 base image (P2/P4: Cloud Hypervisor has Rust-native qcow2 backing-chain support since v34 - no QEMU runtime dependency), and extend the durable worktree->VM binding chain to worktree->VM->volume in PostgreSQL. Raw for the durable volume and qcow2 only for the disposable delta is a deliberate crash-consistency split (P9: raw files have no metadata to corrupt; the delta's corruption remedy is 'discard and re-derive'). The source worktree stays virtio-fs read-mostly, and durability-critical writes THROUGH virtio-fs are FORBIDDEN: P1 documents virtiofsd as a per-VM sidecar daemon with no reconnect story (Kata #2315: daemon death hangs the guest mount and kills the sandbox; Kata #2797 catalogs a crash-mode family) - the volume, never the shared directory, is the durability layer for work products.

VERIFIED BASELINE (WP-1 branch, lands on main after merge): today's persistent VM boots with NO disk device at all - persistent_boot_args (sandbox/cloud_hypervisor/adapter.rs ~1713-1753) emits only --api-socket/--kernel/--initramfs/--cmdline/--serial/--console/--cpus/--memory, and the initramfs comment at adapter.rs ~663 states there is no virtio-fs/virtio-pci in the per-exec guest. Both --disk wiring and any virtio-fs worktree share are net-new surfaces; this MT adds ONLY the virtio-blk --disk surface and states the virtio-fs policy for whichever MT later adds the share.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: adapter.rs gains a typed disk-attachment surface threaded into persistent_boot_args; workspace_volumes/ gains volume_provisioning.rs (raw ext4 creation, qcow2 delta derivation, attachment planning); one new migration 03NN_workspace_volume_bindings.sql; WorktreeVmRegistry ensure-path gains an optional volume-attachment spec; tests including at least one REAL Cloud Hypervisor VM boot with an attached volume (Spec-Realism Gate: this MT declares real VM/disk resources).

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Typed disk surface (adapter.rs + workspace_volumes/volume_provisioning.rs):
   pub enum VmDiskKind { NamedVolumeRaw, BootDeltaQcow2 { backing_image_digest: Sha256Digest } }
   pub struct VmDiskAttachment { pub host_path_rel: String, pub kind: VmDiskKind, pub readonly: bool }
   persistent_boot_args appends, per attachment, "--disk" + "path=<abs_wsl_path>[,readonly=on]" after the --memory pair (adapter.rs ~1748-1750), converting the runtime-root-relative host path through the same Windows->WSL path plumbing the adapter already uses (warm_agent_package.rs windows_path_to_wsl ~708). Base images attach readonly=on; the delta and the named volume attach writable. Attachment order is deterministic: delta boot disk first, named volume second, so guest device names are stable (/dev/vda delta, /dev/vdb volume).
2. Volume creation (volume_provisioning.rs):
   pub struct WorkspaceVolumeSpec { pub workspace_id: String, pub volume_name: String, pub size_bytes: u64 }
   volume_name validated ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ (no spaces, disk-agnostic); layout <runtime_root>/workspace_volumes/volumes/<workspace_id>/<volume_name>.raw and .../deltas/<workspace_id>/boot-gen<N>.qcow2 (MT-321 runtime root; NEVER inside a repo worktree - reuse the MT-321 guard).
   pub async fn create_named_volume(spec) -> Result<ProvisionedVolume, VolumeError>  // create sparse raw file (File::set_len), then mkfs.ext4 -q via the adapter's existing WSL launcher shape (`wsl.exe -d <distro> -e mkfs.ext4 ...`, config surface CloudHypervisorConfig distro/wsl_exe accessors adapter.rs ~417-425); fsync file + parent dir; idempotent: an existing registered volume file is returned, never re-mkfs'd (re-mkfs of a live volume is data loss).
   pub async fn derive_boot_delta(base: &BaseImageRecord, workspace_id, generation) -> Result<PathBuf, VolumeError>  // write a minimal qcow2 v3 empty-delta file whose header references the base blob path (CH consumes backing chains natively, P2); primary path is a small Rust qcow2-v3 header writer validated by booting CH against it; recorded fallback: shell out to qemu-img create -f qcow2 -b when present (tool-presence probed, never required). Never open the base blob for write (MT-321 AC-321-7; P4).
3. Registry extension, migration 03NN_workspace_volume_bindings.sql (append-only; 0365 is never edited):
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workspace_volume_bindings (
       volume_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
       binding_id UUID,                      -- current worktree_vm_bindings.binding_id when attached; NULL when detached
       worktree_id TEXT NOT NULL,
       volume_name TEXT NOT NULL,
       volume_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (volume_kind IN ('named_raw', 'boot_delta_qcow2')),
       backing_image_digest TEXT CHECK (backing_image_digest IS NULL OR backing_image_digest ~ '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'),
       host_path_rel TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (host_path_rel !~ '\s' AND host_path_rel !~ '^[A-Za-z]:' AND left(host_path_rel, 1) <> '/'),
       size_bytes BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (size_bytes >= 0),
       delta_generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
       volume_state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (volume_state IN ('provisioning', 'detached', 'attached', 'quarantined')),
       generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
       owner_account_id UUID NOT NULL,
       actor_principal_id UUID NOT NULL,
       authenticated_session_id UUID NOT NULL,
       access_space_id UUID NOT NULL,
       workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       CONSTRAINT uq_workspace_volume_name UNIQUE (owner_account_id, workspace_id, volume_name),
       CONSTRAINT chk_delta_has_backing CHECK (volume_kind <> 'boot_delta_qcow2' OR backing_image_digest IS NOT NULL)
   ); plus model_lane_resource_scope_registry registration (0365 lines 38-40 pattern) and an index on (owner_account_id, workspace_id, volume_state). The chain worktree->VM->volume resolves as workspace_volume_bindings.binding_id -> worktree_vm_bindings (0365 lines 8-30) -> live handle via the owning adapter; backing_image_digest -> base_image_registry is the P4 child edge that MT-321's has_children seam and MT-326's GC mark phase read.
   Rust: pub struct WorkspaceVolumeRegistry { pool: PgPool, access: ResourceAccessContext } mirroring WorktreeVmRegistry::new_durable (worktree_vm_registry.rs ~214-225); attach/detach transitions update binding_id + volume_state with generation increment; all reads scope-filtered (resource_scope.rs sql_predicate ~798).
4. Attachment flow: extend the ensure path (worktree_vm_registry.rs ensure_worktree_vm_with_spec ~268; worktree_spec ~232 currently sets binds: vec![]) with an optional Vec<VmDiskAttachment> carried through ProcessSpec metadata or a new spec field; the per-worktree mutex already held across spawn + durable write also covers the volume attach row-write so a crash cannot leave a VM up with an unrecorded attachment. Detach on teardown transitions volume_state -> 'detached', binding_id -> NULL; the raw file is NEVER deleted by teardown (deletion authority is exclusively MT-326's lease-fenced GC).
5. virtio-fs policy (P1, binding on later MTs): when a worktree share device is added, it mounts read-mostly; guest tooling MUST write work products, outbox content (MT-324), and anything promised durable onto the virtio-blk volume; a documented guest convention (/hsk-volume mount point) plus a policy test in this MT asserting the attachment planner never marks a virtio-fs-backed path as a durability target.
6. RESOURCE PRIVACY NOTE: volume rows carry the five scope columns (resource_scope.rs ~854-858) and are stamped/filtered exactly like MT-321 registry rows; a volume derived from a base image inherits scope via ResourceScope::derive_from_sources (~193-228) - mixed-scope derivation refuses rather than widens (HBR-PRIV-004); cross-account volume visibility is a live-tested denial.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read adapter.rs persistent_boot_args (~1713-1753), spawn_persistent (~1764+), CloudHypervisorConfig accessors (~417-520), and worktree_vm_registry.rs ensure/teardown paths (~232-320, ~721-935) on post-merge main.
2. Implement VmDiskKind/VmDiskAttachment and thread --disk args into persistent_boot_args with a unit test over the generated arg vector (mirror the existing ch_remote_args_shape test style, adapter.rs ~7008).
3. Implement runtime-root layout + create_named_volume (sparse file + WSL mkfs.ext4 + fsync) and derive_boot_delta (Rust qcow2-v3 empty delta writer; CH boot is the integration proof).
4. Write and apply migration 03NN_workspace_volume_bindings.sql against real PostgreSQL.
5. Implement WorkspaceVolumeRegistry with attach/detach transitions and scope enforcement.
6. Wire optional attachments through the ensure path under the existing per-worktree mutex; teardown detaches and never deletes.
7. Tests: real-VM boot with delta+volume attached, guest mounts /dev/vdb ext4 rw and a written marker survives VM teardown + volume reattach to a fresh VM; delta discard-and-rederive keeps the named volume intact; re-provision idempotency never re-mkfs; scope denial; no-delete-on-teardown proof.
8. Run proof targets under scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR; record measured output.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/migrations/0365_worktree_vm_bindings.sql (append-only migration discipline; extend via new table, never edit)
session_worktrees/** and any repo worktree path (volume bytes live under the product runtime root only)
acceptance_criteria: AC-322-1: persistent_boot_args emits deterministic --disk entries (delta first, named volume second; base-backed content readonly=on where attached) and a unit test locks the generated arg vector shape; the no-disk baseline behavior is unchanged when no attachments are requested.

AC-322-2: create_named_volume produces a sparse raw ext4 image under <runtime_root>/workspace_volumes/volumes/<workspace_id>/<volume_name>.raw with validated no-space names; re-provisioning an existing registered volume is idempotent and NEVER re-runs mkfs (live test proves data survives a second ensure).

AC-322-3: derive_boot_delta produces a qcow2 delta backed by an MT-321 base blob without ever opening the base for write; a REAL Cloud Hypervisor VM boots from the delta chain (Spec-Realism Gate: real VM/disk proof declared and required).
AC-322-4: A guest-written marker on the named volume survives VM teardown and is readable after reattaching the volume to a fresh VM (real-VM round-trip test).
AC-322-5: Deleting or corrupting the delta and re-deriving (delta_generation increment) leaves the named volume byte-identical (discard-and-rederive test, P9 remedy).

AC-322-6: Migration creates workspace_volume_bindings with scope columns, uq_workspace_volume_name, chk_delta_has_backing, and model_lane_resource_scope_registry registration; applied against real PostgreSQL; worktree->VM->volume resolves via binding_id join to worktree_vm_bindings.

AC-322-7: Attach/detach transitions run under the same per-worktree mutex as VM spawn/teardown; teardown detaches (binding_id NULL, state 'detached') and a negative test proves the raw volume file still exists afterward - no deletion path exists in this MT.

AC-322-8: The attachment planner refuses to designate any virtio-fs-backed path as a durability target (typed error + policy test); the /hsk-volume guest convention is documented in the UserManual entry.

AC-322-9: Cross-account volume reads are denied (live two-account test); volume rows are stamped via ResourceAccessContext and filtered via sql_predicate; derived-volume scope uses derive_from_sources and a mixed-scope attempt refuses rather than widens.
AC-322-10: No SQLite, no Docker/containerd dependency, no --force deletes, no absolute paths or spaces in stored paths; grep proofs pass; implementer never marks COMPLETED.

real-VM test: boot delta+volume chain; guest mounts ext4 volume rw
real-VM test: marker written in guest survives teardown and reattach to a fresh VM
test: delta discard + re-derive leaves named volume byte-identical

implementation_notes: Field basis: P1 (virtio-fs crash modes - never the durability layer), P2 (virtio-blk raw/qcow2, CH Rust-native qcow2 + backing since v34, Firecracker's deliberate virtio-blk-only stance), P4 (backing chains, never write to a base with children, keep chains shallow: exactly base->delta, depth 1), P7 (Docker model: read-only base + disposable writable layer + named durable volume), P9 (raw for durable volume, qcow2 only for disposable delta).

WSL caveat from research Area 1: volume files must live on the WSL-ext4-visible runtime root, and 'host crash' includes wsl --shutdown teardown; the deep-durability proofs (kill VMM, wsl --shutdown) are MT-323/MT-328 scope - this MT only proves clean-teardown survival.

Spec-Realism Gate: this MT declares real VM/disk resources - AC-322-3/4/5 must run against a real Cloud Hypervisor VM under WSL; fake-adapter-only proof is insufficient. PG proofs run against real PostgreSQL.

The qcow2-v3 empty-delta writer is deliberately minimal (header + backing-file reference, no data clusters); CH booting from the derived chain IS its validation. Record the writer-vs-qemu-img decision and probe results in the implementation evidence.

House rules: all Rust; PostgreSQL/EventLedger authority, no SQLite; no Docker/containerd/K8s deps; disk-agnostic relative stored paths, no spaces; volume files under product runtime root, never repo worktrees; no --force deletes; implementer never marks COMPLETED.

Resource privacy: volumes, and everything later derived from them (bundles, manifests), stay inside the owning account/Principal scope; reuse resource_scope.rs primitives - never hand-rolled WHERE clauses.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend provisioning MT; the operator-facing volume surface (sizes, states, quota pressure) is MT-327. Provisioning state is reconstructable from workspace_volume_bindings rows and MT-327's FR events.

target_entries: Workspace volumes > Named durable volumes (raw ext4, /hsk-volume guest mount convention, what survives VM teardown)
Workspace volumes > Boot deltas (disposable qcow2, discard-and-rederive remedy, base image chains)
Workspace volumes > virtio-fs policy (worktree share is read-mostly; durability-critical writes go to the volume)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: DW-family FR kinds (volume created/attached/detached) are introduced centrally in MT-327; until then, workspace_volume_bindings rows with generation counters are the reconstruction surface. Record DEFERRED-to-MT-327.
Emit diagnostic events on mkfs failure, qcow2 derivation failure, and attach/detach row-write failure via the open diagnostic-event API if present; otherwise DEFERRED-with-reason.
Provisioning operations are short-lived subprocess/SQL steps; VM liveness itself is already covered by the WP-1 handle/lease machinery, not this MT.

risk_if_missed: Agent work products live only inside disposable VM state or ride virtio-fs (whose sidecar crash modes hang the mount): a VMM or host crash silently destroys completed agent work, and MT-323..326 have no durable disk, no binding chain, and no handoff source to build on.

risks: RISK-1: Idempotent-provision regression re-runs mkfs.ext4 on an existing populated volume, wiping all agent work while reporting success.
RISK-2: The delta writer or attachment code opens the base image blob for write, silently corrupting every workspace backed by that toolchain image (P4).

RISK-3: Teardown or a cleanup sweep deletes the raw volume file (treating it like disposable VM scratch under the adapter work_dir), destroying un-promoted work - the exact failure class the whole DW family exists to prevent.

RISK-4: A crash between VM spawn and the attach row-write (or vice versa) leaves a VM holding a volume with no registry record, making the volume invisible to leases/GC fencing and to the operator surface.
RISK-5: Durability-critical outputs are routed through the virtio-fs share because it is convenient, reintroducing the P1 crash-mode family.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): create_named_volume checks registry + file existence before mkfs; live test writes data, re-ensures, and proves bytes survive; mkfs only ever runs on a freshly created sparse file.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): delta derivation opens the base path read-only; MT-321's write-to-base tripwire extends to this module; real-VM boot proves the readonly attachment.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): no code path in this MT unlinks a .raw volume; teardown test asserts file existence afterward; deletion authority exists only in MT-326 behind lease fencing.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): attach row-write happens under the same per-worktree mutex and ordering as the WP-1 spawn+durable-write path; a crash-injection test proves the reconcile-visible states are only (recorded+attached) or (recorded+detached), never (attached+unrecorded).
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): attachment planner types virtio-fs paths as non-durability targets and refuses; policy test is a named regression; guest convention documented in the manual.

research_provenance.source: Research basis: .GOV/reference/wp_kernel_017_expansion_research/expansion-research-20260814.json, catalog durable_volumes_and_handoff, patterns P1 (virtiofsd crash modes; Kata #2315/#2797), P2 (virtio-blk raw/qcow2; CH Rust-native qcow2 backing since v34; io_uring qcow2 backend v51), P4 (backing chains; never write to a base with children), P7 (Docker reference model), P9 (raw durable volume vs disposable qcow2 delta), plus Area-1 WSL caveats. Verified current code on the WP-1 feature branch worktree wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 (paths land on main after WP-1 merges; frozen candidate df463aa6): sandbox/cloud_hypervisor/adapter.rs persistent_boot_args ~1713-1753 (NO --disk today), spawn_persistent ~1764+, CloudHypervisorConfig ~394-520, no-virtio-fs comment ~663, ch_remote_args ~4880; swarm_orchestration/worktree_vm_registry.rs worktree_spec ~232 (binds vec![], NetPolicy::DenyAll), ensure_worktree_vm_with_spec ~268, teardown_worktree_vm ~721, new_durable ~214-225; migrations/0365_worktree_vm_bindings.sql lines 8-40; warm_agent_package.rs windows_path_to_wsl ~708.
corrections: Operator constraints baked in: no QEMU/Docker/containerd runtime dependency (qemu-img allowed only as a probed optional fallback for delta creation, never required); no SQLite; no --force deletes; deletion authority reserved to MT-326.
Backing chains are fixed at depth 1 (base -> delta) per P4's deep-chain warning; deeper layering is out of scope and must not be added opportunistically.
